cases.answer:
Based only on the extracted text from the evaluator-provided URLs:

- **Readers concurrent with a writer: yes.** SQLite states that “writers and readers can run at the same time” in WAL mode. [SQLite WAL — Concurrency](https://sqlite.org/wal.html#concurrency)
- **Two writers committing at the same time to the same database: no.** There can be “only one writer at a time”; writes are serialized, so writers take turns. [SQLite WAL — Concurrency](https://sqlite.org/wal.html#concurrency) [SQLite — Isolation Between Database Connections](https://sqlite.org/isolation.html)
- **An already active read transaction immediately seeing another connection’s new commits: no.** WAL provides snapshot isolation: commits made while the read transaction is active remain invisible to it. To see them, the reader must end its transaction and start a new one. [SQLite — Isolation And Concurrency](https://sqlite.org/isolation.html)

The extracted documentation supports all three points; there is no evidence gap for these questions.
